_comment: THE ROOM. Everything here is a property of the space, not of the rig -- so a
new room is a new venue file and nothing else changes. Millimetres, y up,
origin at the front-left floor corner.
crowd_zone and canopy are consumed by the beam-aware intensity taper (F4).
They are the answer to the two things that actually went wrong on the night:
beams caught people in the eye, and the parachute clipped the aerials' throw.
MEASURE THESE ON SITE. The numbers below are the despacio room as built, and
the head band is a stated assumption rather than a measurement -- see its
ROOM GREW 2026-08-07. The rig does not hang on the walls: it hangs on a
truss frame standing in the middle of a room twice as long and twice as
wide, with a ceiling half again as high. The truss rectangle below is
exactly where the walls used to be modelled, so the rig's own geometry --
the 9.144 m square it is rigged on, the ball in the middle of it, the heads
500 mm inboard of the bar -- is unchanged; every coordinate simply moved
4572 mm in x and z because the origin is still the ROOM's front-left floor
corner and the room now starts 4572 mm further out on each side.
The canopy did NOT move. It is still rigged at 4600 mm, which is now well
below the ceiling rather than flush with it.
name: despacio room
_ball_radius_comment: A mirror ball is a SOLID sphere, so it genuinely blocks a beam rather than
scattering all of it onward. The safety taper models that occlusion, and
that is most of why the ball poses were safe on a rig with no safety system
at all -- without it the taper would dim the show's signature look for no
300 mm radius (a 24-inch ball) was set by hand on 2026-08-07, replacing an
estimated 200. Still not measured. Measure the real one: too large and the
taper trusts an occlusion that is not there, and this is the direction that
errs toward NOT dimming -- a bigger ball here means the taper believes more
beams are blocked than really are.
_apex_comment: The point directly above the ball that the aerial poses converge on. With a
parachute rigged this is the canopy height and the beams land ON it and it
glows; without one it is the ceiling.
These were the same number while the ceiling was 4600. They are not any
more: unrig the canopy and this must be raised to 6900 by hand, or every
aerial pose will be computed as stopping 2.3 m short of what it now hits.
_truss_comment: WHAT THE RIG HANGS ON. A rectangular frame of bar standing free in the
room, not against its walls -- min/max are the bar's CENTRELINE, height is
the centre of its section, and `bar` is how thick that section is.
`bar` is 60 mm -- a single thin pole, not box truss. It is the previz's
whole physical model of the structure, so if the real thing is a 290 mm
box section, say so here; nothing but the drawing depends on it.
This is the 9.144 m square the show was designed around: before 2026-08-07
the model had walls here, and every measurement in rig.json is still taken
from this rectangle (the heads sit 500 mm inboard of it, at bar height).
So if the room is ever re-measured, this frame is the thing to keep fixed
relative to the fixtures -- the walls can go anywhere.
The safety taper ignores it deliberately. A bar is thin, it is above the
head band, and the taper's job is people's eyes; the previz DOES give it
collision, so a beam aimed into it stops there as it really would.
_crowd_zone_comment: Where people stand, and how high their eyes are. The taper drives intensity
to zero for any beam whose cone enters the head band inside this footprint,
with a soft edge outside it.
head_band_min/max is 1.4-2.0 m: roughly seated-tall to standing-tall. It is
a judgement call, not a measurement, and it is deliberately generous at the
top -- someone on someone's shoulders is exactly who gets hit. Raising the
floor of the band buys back throw at the cost of catching shorter people.
The footprint is inset from the TRUSS, not from the walls -- the corners
hold the heads themselves and nobody stands in them. It did not grow when
the room did: people stand under the rig, not out in the far corners.
Widen it here if that stops being true, because a beam over somebody
standing outside this box is not tapered at all.

_strobe_comment: Photosensitive epilepsy is the one genuine medical risk on this rig, and
unlike dazzle from a beam there is no aversion response to fall back on.
NOT a frequency limit. The MJ-OS-018's profile declares its shutter as
'Strobe slow to fast' with no Hz at either end, so the engine drives a
normalised position within that band and genuinely does not know what rate
a given value produces. A number in Hz here would be invented to look
'ceiling' caps how far up that band anything may drive the shutter. Faster
is further up the band on every fixture that has one, so this is an honest
proxy for 'not the fast end' without knowing the mapping.
'max_seconds' caps CONTINUOUS strobe, which is what the guidance is
actually about -- a one-bar hit is a very different thing from ninety
seconds of it -- and it holds whatever the rate turns out to be. The
shutter must then stay open for 'recover_seconds' before another burst is
allowed, so the cutoff is a stop rather than a duty cycle.
Set conservatively as a starting point. These are NOT measured, and the
